checks.output-reproducible: Source with run instructions, a usable public demo, or published weights/data are alternatives, not cumulative requirements; a bare openness assertion without a usable link is only claimed.
checks.acceptance-criteria-defined: A metric/threshold, pass-fail suite or named benchmark are alternatives. Do not demand numerical thresholds for every alternative or require results for a definition.
checks.acceptance-criteria-met: A score alone is not a met criterion: identify the bar and linked result/report/register. A badge without a verifiable ID/register remains claimed; leave live verification to confirmation.
checks.failure-modes-tested: Separate a tested named failure plus observed behaviour from a robustness promise. A report is cited where available, not an additional mandatory artefact.
checks.operational-owner-assigned: A responsible role, team or support contact can qualify; no named individual or formal on-call process is required. Bare maintenance claims do not identify ownership.
checks.assurance-defined: Identify an ongoing mechanism and its named failure-mode connection. Monitoring, recurring review or audit are alternatives; generic security or badges alone are insufficient.
checks.support-maintenance-defined: Any one help channel, cadence or approval process suffices; no SLA or link is mandatory. Legal/privacy/sales-only contacts and unexplained bare links do not establish product help.
checks.outcome-measure-defined: Identify the specific tracked outcome, not generic impact. Units/capture methods are specificity examples, not universally mandatory fields. Technical metrics need the stated outcome context.
checks.baseline-defined: A before value, control group or prior-period figure can qualify. Identify the counterfactual actually used; an unanchored improvement claim is insufficient.
checks.outcome-measured: Use an observed after-value, not a target or qualitative improvement claim. Do not impose the separate baseline check here; link an artefact only where one exists.
checks.important-confounds-named: Caveats must relate to the comparison. A relevant stated confidence interval can qualify; neither formal causal design nor several confounds is mandatory.
checks.outcome-evidence-available: Identify the measured result and baseline relied on for this decision. Generic demos/data are insufficient; referencing or quoting relevant evidence need not add an external report.
checks.full-cost-accounted: Require a stated figure explicitly naming multiple relevant components, not an inferred boundary. Build-plus-operation is an example, not the only eligible pair.
checks.risk-tradeoffs-assessed: Distinguish a material decision-related risk/trade-off from an unrelated feature limit. One named consideration suffices; no numerical score or formal report is required.
checks.alternatives-compared: Name a specific alternative actually considered and why rejected. Status quo qualifies; competitor lists or feature differences alone do not show a decision comparison.
checks.value-rule-explicit: Identify the actual decision rule, not an unrelated alert threshold or post-hoc satisfaction. Explicit informal rules can qualify without a numerical threshold or formal preregistration.
